questions.q: What does the editorial ask of political parties once an election is over?
options: To withdraw from public life if defeated
Not quite. The article says: To stop treating each other as rivals and work together for the country’s good.
To stop treating each other as rivals and work together for the country’s good
Yes. Like sportsmen after a match.
To prepare at once for the next contest
Not quite. The article says: To stop treating each other as rivals and work together for the country’s good.
To challenge the result in every way
Not quite. The article says: To stop treating each other as rivals and work together for the country’s good.
questions.rationale: “The party that has lost must accept its defeat without any sense of humiliation, while the winning party must take its victory without pride… All parties should focus on a single goal, that is, national development.”

questions.article: The Form and Spirit of Ramazan
questions.q: In form Ramazan is a month of fasting. What does the article say it is in spirit?
options: A month of feasting at night
Not quite. The article says: A month of self-training and introspection in the light of the Quran.
A month of travel to holy places
Not quite. The article says: A month of self-training and introspection in the light of the Quran.
A month of self-training and introspection in the light of the Quran
Right. The Quran is like a mirror.
A month of rest from all work
Not quite. The article says: A month of self-training and introspection in the light of the Quran.
questions.rationale: “In terms of form, the month of Ramazan is the month of fasting. But, in terms of spirit, the month of Ramazan is a month of self-training.”

questions.article: The Form and Spirit of Ramazan
questions.q: “God does not change the condition of a people’s lot, unless they change what is in their hearts” (13:11). What does the article say a sincere reader draws from this verse?
options: That complaint against others is useless; reform must begin with oneself
Yes. Then divine help follows.
That only leaders need to change
Not quite. The article says: That complaint against others is useless; reform must begin with oneself.
That nothing can ever change
Not quite. The article says: That complaint against others is useless; reform must begin with oneself.
That change must be forced on others
Not quite. The article says: That complaint against others is useless; reform must begin with oneself.
questions.rationale: “He will realize that one has to completely abandon the language of complaint and protest against others… our own reform is the precondition enshrined in the Quran.”

questions.q: What makes a religious act lose its value, according to the article?
options: Performing it briefly
Not quite. The article says: Mixing in a personal motive, such as a wish for fame or to be thought noble.
Performing it without being asked
Not quite. The article says: Mixing in a personal motive, such as a wish for fame or to be thought noble.
Performing it alone
Not quite. The article says: Mixing in a personal motive, such as a wish for fame or to be thought noble.
Mixing in a personal motive, such as a wish for fame or to be thought noble
Correct. Only God and the person know the intention.
questions.rationale: “If one performs a religious act by adding some other, personal motive in it… the action becomes devoid of sincerity. It will have no value in God’s eyes.”

questions.q: A farmer whose land has turned barren begins by preparing the soil, not by harvesting. How does the article apply this to the renewal of a community?
options: Begin by building larger institutions
Not quite. The article says: Begin with reviving the spirit and awakening minds, not with political power or outward forms.
Begin with reviving the spirit and awakening minds, not with political power or outward forms
Well read. Otherwise the cart is put before the horse.
Begin by choosing new leaders
Not quite. The article says: Begin with reviving the spirit and awakening minds, not with political power or outward forms.
Begin by isolating the community
Not quite. The article says: Begin with reviving the spirit and awakening minds, not with political power or outward forms.
questions.rationale: “If they start by reviving the spirit of religion, awakening the soul, and bringing about intellectual development, then it will be a right beginning.”

questions.q: What strength of character does the month of fasting aim to build?
options: Fortitude and self-restraint – staying steady and positive under provocation and hardship
Yes. Training for a whole life of patience.
Indifference to other people
Not quite. The article says: Fortitude and self-restraint – staying steady and positive under provocation and hardship.
Physical toughness for hard labour
Not quite. The article says: Fortitude and self-restraint – staying steady and positive under provocation and hardship.
Skill in debate
Not quite. The article says: Fortitude and self-restraint – staying steady and positive under provocation and hardship.
questions.rationale: “In essence, it is training for a whole life of self-denial, inculcating patience, fortitude and forbearance.”

questions.q: How, according to the article, can someone today experience the Prophet’s companionship?
options: By sincerely following his way – for instance, treating an opponent as he would have done
Right. It depends on inner affinity, not physical presence.
By collecting old manuscripts
Not quite. The article says: By sincerely following his way – for instance, treating an opponent as he would have done.
By dreaming of him
Not quite. The article says: By sincerely following his way – for instance, treating an opponent as he would have done.
By visiting his city once
Not quite. The article says: By sincerely following his way – for instance, treating an opponent as he would have done.
questions.rationale: “Companionship is not necessarily about being physically present with someone. It depends entirely on psychological compatibility.”

questions.q: The material world is orderly while the human world is full of problems. How does the article explain the difference?
options: The universe was made to support man; man was given total freedom, and its misuse causes the problems
Yes. Paradise is given on merit after this test.
The material world is older and so wiser
Not quite. The article says: The universe was made to support man; man was given total freedom, and its misuse causes the problems.
The Creator made the human world carelessly
Not quite. The article says: The universe was made to support man; man was given total freedom, and its misuse causes the problems.
Problems are an illusion
Not quite. The article says: The universe was made to support man; man was given total freedom, and its misuse causes the problems.
questions.rationale: “It is this total freedom that creates all kinds of problems and not creation itself.”

questions.q: Where does the article say the worth of parenting is really tested?
options: In the comfort of the home
Not quite. The article says: Outside the home, in how the child meets life’s challenges.
In the child’s school marks alone
Not quite. The article says: Outside the home, in how the child meets life’s challenges.
Outside the home, in how the child meets life’s challenges
Exactly. Self-confidence is the best gift.
In how much the parents spend
Not quite. The article says: Outside the home, in how the child meets life’s challenges.
questions.rationale: “It is not inside the home that parenting may be judged good or bad. It is outside the home that parenting must be judged.”

questions.article: Learning About Life from the Family
questions.q: The article calls the family a training school. What condition does it set for learning from it?
options: To live apart from them
Not quite. The article says: To look at one’s own family members as objectively as one looks at others.
To obey the eldest in everything
Not quite. The article says: To look at one’s own family members as objectively as one looks at others.
To look at one’s own family members as objectively as one looks at others
Well reasoned. Without idolising them or hiding their faults.
To keep family matters secret
Not quite. The article says: To look at one’s own family members as objectively as one looks at others.
questions.rationale: “You must not idolize your family. You should view your family in just the same way as you view other people.”
